claims.exact_statement: Let C*>=0 and let f be Boolean with m>=2 relevant coordinates such that H(f_{i,s}) <= C* I(f_{i,s}) for every relevant i and s in {+1,-1}, and r=H(f)/I(f) > C*. Then for every relevant i: (a) Delta_i(f) >= C* Inf_i(f) + (r-C*) I(f) > r Inf_i(f); (b) B_i(f) > (r-2/ln 2) Inf_i(f) and Inf_i(f) < e^3 2^{-r}; (c) H(f)-B(f) <= (2/ln 2 - (m-1)(r-C*)) I(f) < (2/ln 2) I(f), so (m-1)(r-C*) <= 2/ln 2 and B(f)/H(f) > 1-2/(r ln 2). If some Boolean function violates H <= C* I, a violator with the fewest relevant variables exists and satisfies the hypotheses.
